Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 1) The most common cause of dysphagia in adults is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Progressive dysphagia in adults should be considered esophageal carcinoma until proven otherwise.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 2) The most common histological type of esophageal carcinoma worldwide is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Squamous cell carcinoma remains the predominant type worldwide, although adenocarcinoma is increasing in Western countries.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 3) The investigation of choice for suspected esophageal carcinoma is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Endoscopy with biopsy provides definitive histological diagnosis.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 4) The most common symptom of carcinoma of the esophagus is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Patients initially develop difficulty swallowing solids, progressing to liquids as the disease advances.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 5) Barrett’s esophagus predisposes to:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Barrett’s esophagus is a premalignant condition resulting from chronic GERD.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 6) The most common cause of Barrett’s esophagus is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Long-standing acid reflux causes intestinal metaplasia of the distal esophagus.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 7) The investigation of choice for GERD is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Endoscopy evaluates reflux esophagitis and detects complications such as Barrett’s esophagus.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 8) The gold standard investigation for confirming GERD is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Twenty-four-hour pH monitoring is the gold standard for documenting pathological acid reflux.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 9) The classical radiological finding in achalasia cardia is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Barium swallow shows smooth tapering of the distal esophagus producing the bird-beak appearance.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 10) The definitive treatment for achalasia cardia in a fit patient is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Laparoscopic Heller’s myotomy with partial fundoplication provides durable symptom relief.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 11) The most common benign tumor of the esophagus is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Leiomyoma is the commonest benign esophageal neoplasm.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 12) The most common symptom of achalasia cardia is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.option2: Dysphagia to both solids and liquids
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Unlike carcinoma, achalasia typically causes dysphagia to solids and liquids from the beginning.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 13) The commonest cause of upper gastrointestinal bleeding is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Peptic ulcer disease remains the leading cause of upper GI hemorrhage.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 14) The most common cause of gastric outlet obstruction in adults is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Although peptic ulcer disease was previously common, gastric malignancy is now the leading adult cause.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 15) The most common site of gastric carcinoma is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: The distal stomach, especially the antrum, is the commonest site of gastric cancer.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 16) The most common histological type of gastric carcinoma is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Over 90% of gastric cancers are adenocarcinomas.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 17) The investigation of choice for suspected gastric carcinoma is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Endoscopy with biopsy confirms the diagnosis and allows histological classification.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 18) Virchow’s node is located in the:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: An enlarged Virchow’s node is a classic sign of advanced gastric carcinoma.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 19) Sister Mary Joseph nodule is a metastatic deposit at the:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: A metastatic umbilical nodule is commonly associated with advanced intra-abdominal malignancies, especially gastric cancer.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 20) Krukenberg tumor refers to:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Krukenberg tumor is a metastatic ovarian tumor, classically arising from diffuse gastric adenocarcinoma.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 21) Which Helicobacter pylori –associated malignancy is well recognized?
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: H. pylori infection is an established risk factor for gastric adenocarcinoma and gastric MALT lymphoma.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 22) The most common site of peptic ulcer is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Duodenal ulcers, particularly in the first part (D1), are more common than gastric ulcers.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 23) The commonest complication of peptic ulcer disease is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Upper gastrointestinal bleeding is the most frequent complication of peptic ulcer disease.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 24) Sudden severe epigastric pain with free air under the diaphragm suggests:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Pneumoperitoneum with acute abdominal pain is highly suggestive of perforation of a hollow viscus.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 25) The investigation showing free air in perforated peptic ulcer is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Free gas under the diaphragm on an erect chest X-ray is a classic finding.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 26) The standard emergency operation for a perforated duodenal ulcer is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Closure with an omental patch followed by H. pylori eradication is the standard treatment.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 27) The most common cause of small bowel obstruction is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Adhesions account for the majority of small bowel obstructions in adults.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 28) The most common cause of large bowel obstruction is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Colorectal cancer is the leading cause of large bowel obstruction in adults.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 29) The classical triad of intestinal obstruction includes:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Absolute constipation is also an important feature, especially in complete obstruction.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 30) The investigation of choice for suspected intestinal obstruction is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: It demonstrates dilated bowel loops and multiple air-fluid levels.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 31) The commonest cause of strangulated intestinal obstruction is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: An incarcerated hernia may compromise bowel blood supply, leading to strangulation.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 32) The most common site of intussusception in children is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Ileocolic intussusception is the commonest type in pediatric patients.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 33) The classical triad of intussusception is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.option1: Colicky pain, red currant jelly stool, palpable abdominal mass
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Although not always present together, this triad is characteristic of intussusception.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 34) The most common site of Meckel’s diverticulum is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: It is located on the antimesenteric border of the ileum, about 2 feet from the ileocecal valve.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 35) Meckel’s diverticulum is a remnant of the:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Failure of involution of the vitelline duct results in Meckel’s diverticulum.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 36) The most common presentation of Meckel’s diverticulum in children is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Ectopic gastric mucosa causes ulceration and painless bleeding.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 37) The investigation of choice for Meckel’s diverticulum with ectopic gastric mucosa is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: The radionuclide scan detects ectopic gastric mucosa within the diverticulum.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 38) The most common cause of acute appendicitis is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Obstruction leads to bacterial overgrowth, inflammation and ischemia.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 39) McBurney’s point is located:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.option1: Junction of the lateral one-third and medial two-thirds of the line joining the right ASIS to the umbilicus
Gastrointestinal Surgery.option4: Midway between the umbilicus and ASIS
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Tenderness at McBurney’s point is a classic sign of acute appendicitis.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 40) The most common complication of acute appendicitis is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Delayed diagnosis increases the risk of appendiceal perforation and generalized peritonitis.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 41) The investigation of choice for suspected acute appendicitis is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Ultrasound is the preferred initial imaging modality, especially in children and pregnant women.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 42) The treatment of uncomplicated acute appendicitis is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Appendicectomy remains the standard treatment for uncomplicated acute appendicitis.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 43) Rovsing’s sign is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.option2: Pain on flexion of the right hip
Gastrointestinal Surgery.option3: Pain on extension of the right hip
Gastrointestinal Surgery.option4: Pain in the right iliac fossa on palpation of the left iliac fossa
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Rovsing’s sign suggests peritoneal irritation in acute appendicitis.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 44) Psoas sign is positive in:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Extension of the right hip stretches the psoas muscle, causing pain in retrocecal appendicitis.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 45) Obturator sign is commonly positive in:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Internal rotation of the flexed hip irritates the obturator internus muscle in pelvic appendicitis.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 46) The most common site of colorectal carcinoma is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: The rectum is the single most common site of colorectal cancer.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 47) The investigation of choice for suspected colorectal carcinoma is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Colonoscopy allows direct visualization, biopsy and evaluation of the entire colon.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 48) The most common tumor marker used in colorectal carcinoma follow-up is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: CEA is mainly used for postoperative surveillance and detection of recurrence.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 49) Iron deficiency anemia in an elderly patient should raise suspicion of:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Occult bleeding from right-sided colon cancer commonly presents with iron deficiency anemia.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 50) The most common presentation of left-sided colon carcinoma is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Left-sided tumors produce annular narrowing, resulting in obstructive symptoms.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 51) Which inherited syndrome has the highest risk of colorectal carcinoma?
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Untreated FAP carries an almost 100% lifetime risk of colorectal cancer.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 52) The gene mutated in Familial Adenomatous Polyposis is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: FAP results from mutation of the APC tumor suppressor gene on chromosome 5.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 53) Lynch syndrome is also known as:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Lynch syndrome results from mismatch repair gene mutations and predisposes to colorectal and several extracolonic cancers.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 54) The most common site of distant metastasis in colorectal carcinoma is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Portal venous drainage makes the liver the most common site of metastasis.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 55) The most common benign anal condition is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Hemorrhoids are enlarged vascular cushions and are the commonest benign anorectal disorder.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 56) Internal hemorrhoids usually occur at:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Primary hemorrhoidal cushions are classically located at the 3, 7 and 11 o’clock positions in the lithotomy position.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 57) The most common symptom of internal hemorrhoids is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Bleeding during or after defecation is the hallmark of internal hemorrhoids.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 58) The most common cause of severe pain during defecation is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: An anal fissure causes intense pain during and after bowel movements.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 59) The most common site of an anal fissure is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Approximately 90% of anal fissures occur in the posterior midline.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 60) The definitive surgical treatment for chronic anal fissure is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Lateral internal sphincterotomy relieves sphincter spasm and promotes fissure healing.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 61) Goodsall’s rule is used to predict the:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.option2: Internal opening of an anal fistula
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Goodsall’s rule predicts the course and internal opening of fistula-in-ano based on the position of the external opening.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 62) The most common cause of fistula-in-ano is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Most anal fistulas develop following an anorectal abscess due to infection of anal glands.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 63) The definitive treatment for fistula-in-ano is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Simple fistulas are treated surgically while preserving sphincter function.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 64) The most common type of anorectal abscess is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Perianal abscess is the commonest anorectal abscess and usually presents with severe perianal pain.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 65) The treatment of anorectal abscess is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Prompt surgical drainage is the treatment of choice. Antibiotics alone are inadequate.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 66) The most common symptom of anal carcinoma is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Patients commonly present with anal pain, bleeding and a palpable ulcerative or fungating lesion.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 67) The most common histological type of anal canal carcinoma is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Squamous cell carcinoma accounts for the majority of anal canal malignancies.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 68) The standard treatment for squamous cell carcinoma of the anal canal is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Combined chemoradiotherapy (Nigro protocol) is the standard treatment, with surgery reserved for persistent or recurrent disease.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 69) The most common complication of hemorrhoidectomy is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Postoperative urinary retention is a frequent early complication due to pain and reflex inhibition.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 70) A thrombosed external hemorrhoid typically presents with:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Acute thrombosis produces sudden severe pain with a tense bluish swelling at the anal margin.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 71) The most common site of diverticular disease is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: The sigmoid colon is the commonest location because of its higher intraluminal pressure.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 72) The most common complication of diverticulosis is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Inflammation of diverticula is the most frequent clinically significant complication.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 73) The most common site of volvulus in adults is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Sigmoid volvulus is the commonest type of colonic volvulus in adults.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 74) The characteristic X-ray finding in sigmoid volvulus is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: A massively dilated sigmoid loop produces the classic coffee-bean appearance on abdominal X-ray.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 75) The initial treatment of uncomplicated sigmoid volvulus is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Flexible sigmoidoscopic decompression is the first-line treatment in the absence of perforation or gangrene.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 76) The most common site of colorectal perforation in diverticulitis is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Diverticulitis most commonly affects the sigmoid colon, where perforation may occur.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 77) The commonest cause of lower gastrointestinal bleeding in the elderly is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Diverticular bleeding is the leading cause of significant lower GI bleeding in older adults.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 78) The most common site of angiodysplasia is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Colonic angiodysplasia most frequently involves the cecum and ascending colon.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 79) Toxic megacolon is a recognized complication of:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Toxic megacolon is a life-threatening complication of severe ulcerative colitis.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 80) The most common extraintestinal manifestation of inflammatory bowel disease is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Peripheral arthritis is the most common extraintestinal manifestation of inflammatory bowel disease.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 81) The most common cause of massive lower gastrointestinal bleeding in adults is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Diverticular disease is the leading cause of painless massive lower GI bleeding in adults.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 82) The most common cause of lower gastrointestinal bleeding in children is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Meckel’s diverticulum commonly presents with painless rectal bleeding in children.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 83) The most common site of Crohn’s disease is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Crohn’s disease most frequently affects the terminal ileum and ileocecal region.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 84) Which inflammatory bowel disease shows skip lesions?
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Crohn’s disease is characterized by discontinuous (“skip”) lesions and transmural inflammation.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 85) Which inflammatory bowel disease is limited to the mucosa?
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Ulcerative colitis causes continuous mucosal inflammation beginning in the rectum.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 86) The most common site involved in ulcerative colitis is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Rectal involvement is almost universal in ulcerative colitis.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 87) The definitive surgical treatment for ulcerative colitis is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Total proctocolectomy removes the diseased colon and rectum, curing ulcerative colitis.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 88) The investigation of choice for diagnosing inflammatory bowel disease is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Colonoscopy with histopathological examination confirms the diagnosis.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 89) The most common benign tumor of the small intestine is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Lipoma is the commonest benign tumor of the small intestine, although benign tumors are overall uncommon.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 90) The most common malignant tumor of the small intestine is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Carcinoid tumors are the most common malignant neoplasm of the small intestine.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 91) The most common site of gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Approximately 60% of GISTs arise in the stomach.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 92) GIST is characteristically positive for:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Expression of CD117 is the characteristic immunohistochemical marker of GIST.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 93) The targeted therapy for unresectable GIST is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Imatinib inhibits the c-KIT tyrosine kinase and is the standard targeted therapy for GIST.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 94) The most common cause of mesenteric ischemia is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Acute embolic occlusion of the superior mesenteric artery is the commonest cause of acute mesenteric ischemia.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 95) Pain out of proportion to physical findings is characteristic of:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Severe abdominal pain with minimal tenderness is the classic presentation of acute mesenteric ischemia.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 96) The investigation of choice for acute mesenteric ischemia is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: CT angiography is the preferred investigation for rapid diagnosis of mesenteric ischemia.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 97) The most common congenital anomaly of the gastrointestinal tract is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Meckel’s diverticulum affects approximately 2% of the population and is the commonest GI congenital anomaly.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 98) Hirschsprung disease results from absence of:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.option2: Ganglion cells in the distal bowel
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Failure of neural crest cell migration leads to aganglionosis and functional intestinal obstruction.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 99) The definitive treatment for Hirschsprung disease is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: The aganglionic segment is resected and normal bowel is pulled through to the anus.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 100) The most common cause of intestinal obstruction in neonates is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Hirschsprung disease is an important cause of neonatal intestinal obstruction and delayed passage of meconium.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 101) The most common symptom of colorectal carcinoma is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: A persistent change in bowel habit is the commonest presenting complaint, particularly in left-sided lesions.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 102) Apple-core lesion on barium enema is characteristic of:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: The annular constricting growth produces the classic apple-core appearance.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 103) The operation of choice for carcinoma of the cecum is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Right hemicolectomy removes the cecum, ascending colon and associated lymphovascular drainage.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 104) The operation of choice for carcinoma of the middle rectum, when sphincter preservation is possible, is:
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Low anterior resection is preferred for mid and upper rectal cancers with adequate distal margins.

Gastrointestinal Surgery.question: 105) Which statement regarding colorectal carcinoma is correct ?
Gastrointestinal Surgery.option2: The lung is the most common site of metastasis.
Gastrointestinal Surgery.option3: Colonoscopy with biopsy is the investigation of choice.
Gastrointestinal Surgery.option4: CEA is recommended for population screening.
Gastrointestinal Surgery.exp: Colonoscopy with biopsy confirms the diagnosis. CEA is mainly used for follow-up, and the liver is the most common site of distant metastasis.
